# A Fixture Paper on Citations

## Introduction

Paradigms shift when anomalies accumulate (1). Lending follows growth (2). The same shift recurs (1).

Several studies agree (2,3). Trust can be measured (3). Networks persist (3).

## Discussion

(2) argue that lending policy follows growth.

## Punctuation and Locators

Anomalies pile up (1)... Is lending growth-led (2)?! Kuhn wrote of "the essential tension" (1). He asked "is it a paradigm?" (1). Lending stalls (in some years (2)).

The pages are cited as a range (3), an open run (3.). A chapter (1) and a section (1).

## Notes and Line Breaks

A prefixed note (see also 3). An abbreviation (e.g., 2). A suffix after a title (3, emphasis added). A wrapped claim (1). A hard break (2)\
on the next line. An ampersand run (3)&more.

Emphasis in affixes (*see* 1, *emphasis added*), and a range (see 3 and *passim*).
